🤖 OpenAI adds Health mode to ChatGPT

OpenAI’s Health mode lets ChatGPT access your medical records and Apple Watch data to answer health questions with real metrics. Users link Apple Health and records from One Medical or Function Health to share tests, medications, visits, sleep, and activity.

ChatGPT compares blood tests, explains medical terms, or suggests allergy-safe restaurants. Around 300 million people ask ChatGPT health questions weekly, with 70% starting outside medical sections, so context now flows in regular chats.

Free users get GPT-5.5 Instant, which flags when a live doctor is needed. Paid users access GPT-5.6 Sol, better at complex cases and explanations.

⚡️Microsoft’s new AI cybersecurity system just hit a 96% score on CyberGym.

That’s 12 points higher than Anthropic’s Mythos while costing roughly half as much as Microsoft’s previous system.

The secret? Microsoft didn’t rely on one giant AI model.

Instead:

• MAI-Cyber-1-Flash handles about 90% of security tasks.
• Only the toughest 10% are escalated to GPT-5.4.

Behind the scenes, a system called MDASH orchestrates 100+ specialized AI agents that:

• Search code for vulnerabilities
• Investigate and debate whether issues are real
• Remove duplicate findings
• Test whether bugs are actually exploitable
• Gather evidence before reporting results

❗️Plot twist: AI isn’t replacing as many workers as companies expected.

For the last year, the message was everywhere: AI agents are coming, jobs are disappearing, and companies are preparing for a much smaller workforce. Now… some of those same companies are quietly hiring again.

Why? Because they discovered something that sounds obvious in hindsight: an AI agent doesn’t replace an employee, it replaces pieces of what that employee does.

A coding AI still needs engineers to tell it what to build, review its code, and fix what it gets wrong.

A sales AI still can’t build trust, read a room, or close every deal. And when AI makes a mistake, guess who gets the phone call? A human.

That’s why companies like Alphabet, Booz Allen, ServiceNow, and even CSX are expanding hiring in key areas instead of shrinking them.

This doesn’t mean the AI job revolution is over. Routine work will continue to disappear, and many roles will change dramatically.

But the companies using AI at scale are learning that the winning strategy isn’t replacing people. It’s pairing the right people with the right AI.
